alt: Text type, audience and purpose together decide the fourth choice, register, which follows from them rather than from the topic. The same topic, school uniform, is formal in an email to the head teacher and informal in a message to a cousin.
caption: Decide text type, audience and purpose; the register follows.

alt: Eight features compared for formal and informal register: address, the form of “you”, contractions, vocabulary, idiom and slang, sentence length, punctuation and the closing. A semi-formal register, as in a school blog post or a speech to your year group, is friendly but careful, with no slang.
caption: Register shows in every feature, from greeting to closing.

alt: Four layout skeletons. Email: subject line, greeting, purpose in the first sentence, a clear request, closing formula, name and role. Blog post: title, date and author, direct address, subheadings and a call for comments. Article: headline, byline, a hook-and-summary opening, facts and quoted comments, an ending that returns to the headline. Diary entry: date, past tenses for events, present for feelings, thoughts about what comes next.
caption: A reader should recognise the text type from its layout alone.

alt: Three columns of conventions. Speech: greet the audience, introduce your point, signposts, rhetorical questions, repetition and lists of three, “you” and “we”, a memorable ending. Brochure or leaflet: title and slogan, headings, bullet points, imperatives, practical details, image space, a call to action. Review: title, key facts, description without spoilers, strengths and weaknesses with evidence, a recommendation and often a rating.
caption: Each text type has conventions its readers or listeners expect.

after: ## Worked example: one topic, three text types
alt: The same food-festival facts written three ways. A formal email to the festival coordinator asks for a stall, opens “Dear Mr Brennan,” avoids contractions and ends with “Yours sincerely” and a role. A semi-formal blog post persuades students to volunteer and ends by asking for comments. An informal diary entry reflects on feelings and ends with a private worry.
caption: The facts stay the same; audience, purpose, register and endings all change.
